clue.text: Beat Peterboro' Utd on pens

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the run of words that follows holds the answer inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the shortened town name, the club abbreviation and the next word

explanation.surface: A football report: Peterborough United win a match in a penalty shoot-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' reads as football slang for penalties; here it is the verb meaning enclose. The apostrophe in Peterboro' only marks the shortening and is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or defeat them, a plain synonym of beat as a verb.

clue.text: One might Google "rotten holiday"

parts.note: food that has gone rotten is off
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: Someone searching the internet for a holiday that went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Google is not the search engine but a cricket verb: to bowl a googly, a leg-spinner's trick ball that turns like an off break. In cricket an off break is a spinning delivery that turns from the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A googly is a disguised delivery that behaves like an off break, so a ball bowled as a googly might be one.

clue.text: Challenger might be fitted with this garment

definitions.text: Challenger might be fitted with this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Challenger is a British army battle tank, and every tank has a top
second meaning: a sleeveless knitted pullover

explanation.surface: A competitor being measured for a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Challenger reads as a rival or contender, but it is the name of a British tank; the second reading is a top fitted to a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless sweater worn over a shirt, an everyday item of clothing.

clue.text: Friend putting on over a stone

indicators.note: putting something on places another item over it, so in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend wears a gemstone over their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone, and gems are commonly called stones.

clue.text: Former Queen award-winning singer tackling Help!

indicators.note: to tackle is to take hold of, so the singer's name wraps around the cry for help

parts.note: the multi-Grammy-winning British singer
aid is help

explanation.surface: A famous singer takes on a Beatles song, with a former queen in the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Help! is a Beatles title, which makes the clue look like a cover version.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Adelaide was wife of King William IV and consort until 1837, so she was once a British queen.

clue.text: Cryptically title old film about animals

parts.note: surface reading: a puzzling heading for some film
setter's reading: the film's name, read as a crossword instruction, means alter slightly; tinker a little with the word little and you get the word title

explanation.surface: Asking for a cryptic name for an old animal film.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1967 musical about a vet who talks to animals; its name splits as doctor (alter) and do little, an instruction that turns LITTLE into TITLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Dolittle is the 1967 film about a physician who can speak with animals.

clue.text: Money, but no yen? Relax!

indicators.note: but no says the following item is left out of the word for money

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
Y is the symbol letter for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Someone told to relax about having no Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge or sprawl lazily, so as a command it can stand for relax.

clue.text: Suitable Dublin or Derry houses

indicators.note: a place that houses something holds it, so the place names contain the answer

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first city, the little word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Is housing in Irish cities like Dublin or Derry suitable?
explanation.definitionFit: Something in order is proper or appropriate for the occasion, an idiom matching suitable.

clue.text: Leave former lover adult film covers

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: a film that covers something wraps round it, so the film's letters go outside

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film
A was an old film certificate for adult viewing

explanation.surface: An ex covers an adult film, before the other one leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Leave is the noun, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is permission for temporary absence, especially leave granted to a boarding school pupil.

clue.text: Complex, intriguing broadcast dragged on, alack

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tangled spy drama on TV went on too long, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloak-and-dagger describes secretive plotting and espionage, so it fits intricate and full of intrigue.

clue.text: A pigeon enthusiast accompanying dog

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: A pigeon fancier out walking with their dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog looks like a noun beside enthusiast; it is the verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The fantail is a breed of domestic pigeon with a spread, fan-shaped tail.

clue.text: Sixteen oz LA California rolls stuffed with Italian food

indicators.note: a roll turns things over, so the concealed run is read from right to left
something stuffed with a filling holds it inside, so the words carry the answer within

parts.note: the run starts at the end of the number and finishes at the start of the state

explanation.surface: A pound of Los Angeles sushi rolls packed with Italian ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: California rolls are sushi, which tempts a food reading; rolls is really the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A calzone is a folded, filled pizza from Italy, so it is an Italian dish.

clue.text: Ceremony regularly hosted by Braintree

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the town is kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the Essex town

explanation.surface: An Essex town holds a ceremony on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal religious or solemn act, a direct synonym for ceremony.

clue.text: US gangster failing to finish bird

indicators.note: not reaching the end means the final letter of the gangster's name is dropped

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago mobster

explanation.surface: An American mobster fails to finish off a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for eating, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Check tide when ebbing

indicators.note: an ebbing sea flows back, so the word for the sea's rise and fall runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to look at the tide as it goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to check and correct it before publication, a synonym of check.

clue.text: Go and get fine cut

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
to etch is to cut lines into a surface

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and collect a good cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetch is to go somewhere and bring something back, exactly go and get.

clue.text: Recorded delivery room for ship

indicators.note: recorded speech is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: delivery is the birth of a baby, which is pronounced the same as the mooring word

explanation.surface: A parcel sent by Recorded Delivery, the UK postal service, to a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Recorded Delivery is a Royal Mail signed-for service, which hides the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is a place where a ship moors, so it is space allotted to a vessel.

clue.text: In Whitechapel, one might step on these fruits

definitions.text: In Whitechapel, one might step on these
definitions.note: the rhyming slang phrase stands for a plural noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Cockney rhyming slang for stairs, used in London's East End
second meaning: two common orchard fruits

explanation.surface: Fruit dropped in an East End street gets trodden on.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitechapel is in London's East End, home of Cockney rhyming slang, where a phrase rhyming with a word replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang the phrase means stairs, which people step on; literally it names two kinds of tree fruit.

clue.text: Breathe audibly like Blackbeard?

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Blackbeard was the notorious pirate Edward Teach

explanation.surface: Breathing noisily like the famous buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: Audibly suggests a sound-alike, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, to aspirate is to pronounce a sound with an audible puff of breath.

clue.text: Expensive leather rips? Just a fake display

parts.note: crocodile skin is a costly luxury leather
tears are rips

explanation.surface: Damage to a pricey leather item turns out to be only for show.
explanation.walkthrough: The rips are tears as in tearing, not crying; the phrase then rereads them as weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodile tears are insincere weeping, a show of sorrow that is not genuinely felt.

clue.text: More dangerous runs beginning to intimidate winter sport fan

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the word
someone keen on skiing

explanation.surface: Steep runs start to frighten a keen skier.
explanation.walkthrough: Runs looks like ski slopes in this setting; it is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskier is the comparative of risky, so it means more hazardous or more dangerous.

clue.text: American airline told to return dishonest character

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
British Airways

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the last word is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American airline is instructed to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad lot is an idiom for a person of poor character, someone untrustworthy or crooked.

clue.text: Frustrate miserable retired husband

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the word for miserable runs backwards

parts.note: sad means miserable
H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife thwarting her gloomy husband now he has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired reads as describing the husband, but it acts on the adjective before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash hopes is to destroy them, so dash means frustrate or thwart.

clue.text: Inside cafeteria, drinking this?

indicators.note: inside points to letters lying within the phrase, here running from that word into the next

parts.note: the last two letters of the first word and the first four of the second

explanation.surface: A guess at what someone sitting in a cafeteria is drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the hiding place and the definition: it is a drink you might order there.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is decaffeinated coffee, the sort of drink commonly ordered in a café or cafeteria.

clue.text: Daughter rejected Sicilian hothead poet

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the volcano's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, literally a hot head

explanation.surface: A daughter turns down a hot-tempered Sicilian suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Hothead suggests a fiery person; it is a mountain spewing heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri was the medieval Italian poet who wrote the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Your setter, behind pub, gets Italian port

indicators.note: behind places one item after another, so the setter's letter follows the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The crossword setter, out behind a pub, reaches an Italian harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari is a seaport city on the Adriatic coast of southern Italy, capital of Apulia.

clue.text: Speak about western influence

indicators.note: about means around, so the verb's letters go round the single letter

parts.note: to say is to speak
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: A talk about Western cultural influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway means power to control or affect others, so it is a synonym of influence as a noun.

clue.text: Murder victim Abraham Lincoln briefly designated?

parts.note: Abe is the familiar short form of Abraham

indicators.note: briefly means in shortened form, so each name is cut down

parts.note: initial letter of the surname

explanation.surface: Was the assassinated President Lincoln named in shorthand?
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln was himself a murder victim, which pulls the solver toward him; the victim wanted is the Bible's first.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abel was killed by his brother Cain, the first murder victim in the Bible.

clue.text: Natter with boring mate beginning to grate

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the short letter pushes inside the word for mate

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, so china means friend
W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is used

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Chatting with a tedious friend starts to irritate.
explanation.walkthrough: Boring reads as dull; it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal chat or gossip, so it means a natter.

clue.text: Plant liable to fail without oxygen

indicators.note: without here has its old sense of outside, so the reworked letters sit around the element
something failing breaks down, so these letters collapse into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A plant is likely to die if it lacks oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: Without means lacking in the surface, but outside in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a flowering garden plant, often blue, used in bedding and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Gosh! Area in remote road where pigs etc are found

indicators.note: in places the exclamation and the area inside the phrase for remote road

parts.note: far means remote
my is an exclamation of surprise like gosh
A is the abbreviation for area
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Surprise at a remote road where pigs and other livestock live.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmyard is the enclosed area around farm buildings, where pigs, hens and other animals are kept.

clue.text: Unfinished second order for barista

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A barista gets a second order and leaves it half made.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is a milky espresso coffee, a drink a customer asks a coffee-shop worker for.
